reason: Mount the motor on the base; it is the only available action and should start the mechanism.
expectation: The motor will be secured to the wave-machine base, ready for the drive parts.

effect: The motor is mounted, ready for the driver.
reason: The eccentric driver seems like the part that can turn the motor's rotation into movement of the cord; it is also the only offered combination.
expectation: The driver will attach to the frame, ready to be connected to the motor and cord.

effect: The off-centre peg will move the cord's end in a circle while the far end stays anchored.
reaction: The explanation makes the driver's purpose clearer.
reason: The belt should connect the motor to the driver; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: The belt will link the motor to the eccentric driver so it can turn.

effect: The belt drive is in place, ready for the cord.
reason: Attach the cord so the driver can move it; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: The cord will be fitted to the wave frame, though it may still need tensioning.

effect: The cord is fitted but loose, so it needs tensioning.
reason: The tension spring should take up the slack; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: The spring will tension the cord while allowing it to move.

effect: The cord is now tensioned, leaving the drive guard as the next available fitting.
reason: Fit the guard over the drive; it is the only offered combination and should protect the moving parts.
expectation: The clear guard will cover the drive while leaving it visible; the machine may still need power.

effect: The drive is guarded but still disconnected from power; the controller is the remaining fitting.
reaction: The clear guard makes the moving parts understandable while keeping fingers away.
reason: Connect the battery and controller to power the machine; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: The motor will run and the eccentric driver will send a wiggle along the cord, possibly at an adjustable speed.

effect: The powered machine sends a disturbance along the cord, and it reflects from the far end; the chapter goal is complete.
reaction: The reflected wiggle is a satisfying result, though I would like to see more of how speed changes it.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the eccentric driver was most worthwhile: its explanation connected circular motion to disturbing the cord, making the finished machine easier to understand.

leastWorthwhile.text: The cord, spring and guard fittings felt predictable in sequence, with only one combination offered at each step.

surprise.text: The disturbance reflecting from the far end added something I had not expected from simply making a wiggle travel along the cord.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the single-option sequence left little room for meaningful decisions.

continue.text: I would be curious to continue if the next chapter lets me explore how changing the speed affects the waves; this chapter explained the mechanism clearly but offered few choices.
